Until Boulder students lose another chance to take control of their city.

Voting has closed for the November 3 election.

Haven’t voted yet?

If you live in Boulder and want to vote here, you can register or update your voter registration at the UMC through Election Day. Bring valid ID; your Buff OneCard is accepted.

Not registered at your Boulder address?

If Boulder is your voting residence, ask the UMC staff to register you or update your residential address. You can get a ballot and vote during that visit. Already registered at your current address? No update is needed.

To vote in Colorado, you must be a U.S. citizen, be 18 by Election Day, have lived in Colorado for at least 22 days before the election, and not be serving a sentence of confinement or detention for a felony conviction. Read the full eligibility rules ↗.

Registered in another Colorado county?

You may keep your home-county registration or update it to your Boulder residence. If you keep your home-county address and need a ballot at the UMC, ask about a statewide ballot; it does not include local races or measures. Your residential registration address determines your local ballot.

Registered in another state?

You can choose to vote in your home state or register in Colorado if you meet Colorado’s eligibility and residency requirements. Vote only once in this election. If you already voted elsewhere, do not vote again in Boulder.

Living in a dorm?

Use your residence hall’s street address and assigned mailbox number, not your dorm room number. Find the county’s CU address instructions ↗.

Where you register is your choice. Colorado voter registration also has income-tax and motor-vehicle residency implications. Read Boulder County’s student voting guidance ↗ or call 303-413-7740. You can also check your registration at Vote.org ↗.
